item.title: Hyperbranched dielectric polymer networks exhibiting giant energy storage density at 250 °C
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Zhaoyu Ran, Manxi Li, Li Meng, Yiwen Zhang, Yuhang Liu, Jun Hu 等8位作者
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74830-2 To overcome charge transfer and achieve efficient capacitive energy storage in dielectric polymers at thermal extremes, hyperbranched networks are designed to expand inter-chain spacing and suppress secondary relaxation, delivering 4.9 J/cm³ energy density with 90% efficiency at 250 °C.

item.title: Non-Hermitian geometry reveals when quantum amplification depends only on start and end points
item.description:
📚 Physics News
In quantum mechanics, the geometry of quantum states has emerged as a powerful framework for understanding phenomena ranging from electrical conductivity to superconductivity. One research direction aims to extend these geometric concepts to non-Hermitian quantum mechanics—where systems can exchange energy with their environment—including the generalization of the Berry phase, a key geometric quantity, to the non-Hermitian case.

item.title: Defect-induced electrostatic anchoring for extreme-temperature power device encapsulation
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Laili Wang, Qi Wang, Yongmei Gan, Yisen Lv, Tianshu Yuan, Dingkun Ma 等7位作者
The transition to wide-bandgap semiconductors requires power electronics to operate reliably at extreme temperatures exceeding 250 °C. Silicone gels are essential for power-device packaging, yet they undergo accelerated dielectric degradation under such severe thermal conditions. Traditional chemical modification methods fail to withstand such extreme temperatures, inevitably compromising long-term reliability. Here, we report a modifier-free 0D/2D hybrid filler architecture within silicone gel constructed via a defect-induced electrostatic anchoring strategy. item.title: Flexible hydrogel fiber-coupled SERS sensor for remote in situ food inspection
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Xinghua Yang, Li Li, Nikolay V Petrov, Chen Shi, Fengjun Tian, Pingping Teng 等16位作者
Optical fiber-based surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensors offer efficient signal transmission and stable Raman enhancement, showing great potential for food safety. However, the rigidity of conventional silica fibers limits direct in situ detection on curved food surfaces, making it challenging to integrate remote signal readout and conformal sampling into a single SERS sensor. This study presents a flexible hydrogel fiber-coupled optical fiber SERS sensor. item.title: Quantum-Accelerated Nonlinear Seismic Simulation for Megathrust-Prone Urban Environments: A Three-Order-of-Magnitude Speedup via HHL-Embedded Newton–Raphson Integration
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 PAUL RICARDO
Background: Nonlinear Time-History Analysis (NLTHA) is the most rigorous procedure for evaluating seismic structural performance, yet its O(N³) computational complexity confines its use to single-building studies, precluding real-time city-scale risk assessment in regions of high seismic hazard. item.title: Semiconductor quantum dots 'reawaken' predicted Rabi oscillations, boosting quantum control
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Physicists at Paderborn University have, for the first time, experimentally demonstrated the so-called "return" of Rabi oscillations in semiconductor quantum dots. The phenomenon, which was first predicted theoretically in 2007, describes the decrease in the emission intensity of the quantum dots, which are initially damped by interactions with the lattice vibrations of a solid (phonons).

item.title: Clean crystal surface lets single molecules hit ultimate quantum limit
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Scientists at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light (MPL) have developed a technique for interrogating molecules on surfaces with spectroscopic precision, thereby reaching the ultimate quantum limit for the first time. With their findings, published in Science, the researchers open new opportunities for the study of molecule-surface interactions and molecular quantum technologies.

item.title: Biological strategies to mitigate the effect of water deficit on morphophysiology of soybean
item.description:

👤 Anderson dos Santos Dias, Luiz Otávio Montera Martins, Davi Lucas Bertolino de Alencar, Victor Garcia Holsbaque, Obadias Alves da Silva, João Pedro Assis Ozório 等9位作者
Water stress is a major constraint to soybean productivity in tropical environments, impairing physiological processes and plant growth. Growth-promoting microorganisms have been proposed as a sustainable strategy to enhance plant tolerance to drought. This study evaluated the effects of inoculation with Bacillus subtilis and Trichoderma harzianum, alone or combined with the microalga Parachlorella sp., on soybean responses to water deficit. The experiment was conducted in a randomized block design with a 2 × 4 factorial arrangement, considering the presence or absence of the microalga and four cultivation conditions: irrigated control, water deficit, water deficit + B. subtilis, and water deficit + T. harzianum. item.title: By-Layer Covalent Organic Structure as a Metal-Free PCET Catalyst for Efficient Oxygen Evolution in Alkaline and Neutral Media
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Soheila Nakhjiri Kamrani, Afshin Pashabadi, Mohammad Joshaghani
The delayed evolution of proton transfer (PT) as the sluggish component of proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) represents a critical limitation in the design of biomimetic artificial leaves. Here, we report a simple metal-free PCET catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) operating in both neutral and alkaline media, realized through successive evolutionary stages of a bilayer covalent superstructure. Graphite/graphene oxide hosts a repetitive porphyrin-based covalent organic structure (COS) assembled via bidentate ethylenediamine (EDA) linkages, functioning as a PCET catalyst in both alkaline and neutral environments.
